sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Cryo-EM structure resolved; N-terminally FLAG-tagged CCR8 formed a functional G-protein complex with Gαi1, Gβ1-HiBiT, Gγ2, and scFv16, confirming receptor folding, membrane trafficking, and G-protein coupling are preserved.
sites.rationale: CCR8 has no native signal peptide; the extracellular N-terminus begins at residue 1 (M) and extends to residue 35 (K), 35 residues from the TM1 boundary at residue 36 — well beyond the ≥3-residue clearance requirement. An exogenous signal peptide was used in the published construct to drive ER translocation; after its cleavage the FLAG tag is displayed at the extracellular face, making insert_after_residue=0 the only possible junction. Three independent papers (L1, L3, L4/L5) all place a tag at this same N-terminal position using two different tag types (FLAG and V5), with the highest-quality evidence (L1) demonstrating functional G-protein complex formation by cryo-EM. Position is topology-derived because no specific residue number is named in any clip for the junction itself. Full-length human CCR8 engineered with an exogenous hemagglutinin signal peptide followed by a FLAG tag at the N-terminus, expressed in insect cells for cryo-EM. CCR8 has no native signal peptide (topology landmarks confirm residue 1 is extracellular); after cleavage of the exogenous HA-SP, the FLAG tag is left at the extracellular N-terminus immediately before residue 1 (M). The construct also carried a C-terminal LgBiT fusion (intracellular). Corroborated by L3 (bovine prolactin signal sequence + V5 tag at N-terminus, full-length CCR8, expression confirmed) and L4/L5 (N-terminal FLAG by gene synthesis, cell-surface expression confirmed by FLAG staining).

sources.claim: For the cryo-EM study, the human CCR8 gene was cloned into a modified pFastBac1 Vector (Invitrogen) with a hemagglutinin signal peptide followed by a Flag tag at the N terminus and fused with a LgBiT subunit ( 43 ) at the C terminus via a 15× GS linker containing a 3C protease cleavage site and 10× His tag.

literature_notes: All five ledger lines converge on a single extracellular tag position: the N-terminal prepend (insert_after_residue=0). L1 and L2 describe the same cryo-EM construct (FLAG at N-terminus, LgBiT at C-terminus); L3 describes a separate construct with an exogenous bovine prolactin signal sequence and V5 tag; L4 and L5 describe a third construct with an N-terminal FLAG generated by gene synthesis. Because CCR8 is a GPCR with no native signal peptide, the extracellular N-terminus (residues 1–35) is the only extracellular terminus available for tagging. The C-terminal LgBiT fusion (L1/L2) is intracellular (residues 305–355 per topology landmarks) and is recorded in other_positions. No ledger line supports any internal extracellular loop insertion for CCR8. ECL1 (93–107), ECL2 (172–195), and ECL3 (264–276) have no qualifying insertion evidence in the ledger and are therefore not proposed as sites.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal LgBiT fusion via 15× GS linker; topology landmarks place residues 305–355 in the intracellular compartment, so this is an intracellular C-terminal fusion, not a surface tag site.
